analysis: Examined the changes in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Server/StandaloneServer.swift. The visible change adds a nonisolated static helper, `minimumGrantBytes(_:)` (head lines ~1080-1082). It builds a per-model serviceability-floor dictionary from `ExistingSlotGrant`. The result is passed as a new `minimumGrantBytes:` argument to `EngineV2KVSizing.resliceGrants` at the following call sites: `reserveKeepsSurvivorsServiceable` (1039-1044), `resliceAndBuildBundle` (1210-1237, including the fallback retry after the assistant reslice floor), and `resliceGrowSurvivors` (1389-1393). `resliceKeepsSlotsServiceable` now reuses the helper (1071-1076). The effect is that the grant computation respects each slot's floor instead of only the final check. This is a KV-sizing and availability-hardening change. It touches no coordinator trust boundary, key material, attestation, encryption, or prefix-cache storage or crypto (T-041 paths such as KVCacheSSD are not touched). Surrounding code is unchanged: native MiMo lifecycle, stop/shutdown, eviction and acquisition paths. One availability note: `Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:)` traps on duplicate model IDs. Slots are keyed by modelId in a dictionary, so duplicates are not plausible. The pre-existing `resliceKeepsSlotsServiceable` already used the same construction. Not verified: the implementation of `EngineV2KVSizing.resliceGrants` with its new `minimumGrantBytes` parameter, which is outside the supplied units. Its handling of floors that sum to more than the fleet budget is unexamined. The post-reslice serviceability guard at 1239 still fails closed. No security regression identified in the supplied lines. Remaining question for integration: confirm that the `EngineV2KVSizing` change is consistent (no overcommit of the fleet KV budget when floors are applied).
